headline: In 1997 the ocean made a sound so loud it was heard 5,000 km away.
slides: US hydrophones in the Pacific, built to track Soviet submarines, picked up something huge.
Ultra-low frequency, rising over about a minute. Sped up 16 times, it went 'bloop'.
Sensors over 5,000 km apart all heard it. Louder than any known animal.
A giant unknown creature was the internet's favourite.
NOAA traced it to an icequake: a huge iceberg cracking off Antarctica.
Icequakes are getting more common as the poles warm.
sources: Sources: NOAA Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory, NOAA Ocean Service 'What is the Bloop?'
